With calendar_event , it returns the event’s existing meeting note or creates one. PATCH /v1/meeting_notes/:meeting_note_id links a full-page meeting note to a calendar event. Both endpoints accept personal access tokens and Workers with a connected calendar. See Using Notion API from a worker for the Worker flow. Full-page meeting notes in block responses The block endpoints return full-page meeting notes as meeting_notes blocks . Meeting notes blocks now include is_full_page , and calendar_event includes the event’s event_id . Meeting note tools in Notion MCP notion-create-meeting-note creates a full-page meeting note, optionally for a calendar event. notion-link-meeting-note-to-calendar-event links an existing meeting note to an event, and notion-convert-to-meetings-database turns a regular database into a Meetings database. See Create a meeting note . November 11, 2026 Faster page webhooks page.created webhook events now arrive right away, usually within a few seconds. Before, they waited about a minute so later changes could be combined into them. The first page.properties_updated event for a page also arrives right away, and later property edits in the next minute are combined into one event. See Event aggregation for details. If you apply templates when creating pages, check the updated steps in Creating pages from templates . Notion MCP is retiring its legacy SSE endpoint If your client connects to https://mcp.notion.com/sse , switch its transport to Streamable HTTP and its URL to https://mcp.notion.com/mcp . The legacy endpoint shuts down on February 23, 2027 . See Migrate from the legacy SSE endpoint . November 10, 2026 Mention or assign a Custom Agent by ID With the View sessions and interact with agents capability, you can now mention a shared Custom Agent in rich text . Use its agent ID or bot user ID for a mention or a people property assignment. Either action can start an agent run. When you read a mention or assignment, the bot user object gives you the agent ID in agent_id and the bot user ID in id . Small session credit usage credits_used in Retrieve a session and Query sessions no longer reads as 0 for sessions that used less than 0.01 credits. Below 0.01, it has at most two significant figures, so 0.004567 credits reads as 0.0045 . From 0.01 up, it still has at most two decimal places. Both rules round down. November 9, 2026 Custom Agents in people properties You can now assign a Custom Agent to a people page property value when you create a page or update page properties . The connection needs the View sessions and interact with agents capability, and the agent must be selected in the connection’s Agent access tab. Assigning an agent can start a run, the same as assigning it in Notion. Page responses now include assigned Custom Agents as bot user objects . Before, they were left out of people arrays. A bot’s avatar_url is now null when its icon isn’t an image URL. At launch, assignments required the agent’s bot user ID, and rich text mentions returned a validation_error . The November 10 update adds support for agent IDs and mentions. List all users still omits Custom Agents. November 5, 2026 Sync health on data source reads Data source list and retrieval responses now include live sync_metadata.health for data sources synced by Notion’s sync platform. Retrieve a database also includes health for each readable data source. When available, metadata includes owner_user_id , resource , and UTC ISO 8601 timestamps in health.checks . If the health lookup fails or times out, the read still succeeds with health: null . Null means health is unavailable, not that the sync is unhealthy. Legacy and worker sync metadata stays unchanged. See sync metadata for the response fields and health states. November 4, 2026 Beta flags and typed view filters in the JavaScript SDK Pass betas to a typed SDK method to opt one request into an API beta . TypeScript now accepts filters, sorts, and quick filters when you create a view . It also checks filters and quick filters on views.update . SDK support : @notionhq/client v5.31.0 . November 3, 2026 Restore past versions in Notion MCP notion-restore-version restores a page or database to how it looked at a past time. See Restore a past version . November 2, 2026 Notion Agent APIs are generally available The Notion Agent APIs are out of beta. If you still use the private alpha routes, they’re deprecated. See Upgrading from the alpha routes for their replacements. Personal agent in the Notion Agent APIs You can now chat with and manage the personal agent (Notion AI) through the Notion Agent APIs with a personal access token. Use notion_ai as the agent_id to start sessions, retrieve the agent, read its insights, and change its name and model. See The personal agent for what it supports. Update an agent Update an agent ( PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id} ) changes an agent’s name, description, model, status, or favorite state in one request. Update agent status is now deprecated. Send status to Update an agent instead. October 30, 2026 Stored sync metadata on data sources Data source list and retrieval responses now include optional stored sync metadata , with documented provider values and ISO 8601 timestamps. Retrieve a database also includes this metadata for each readable data source. Notion-flavored Markdown becomes the default in the next Notion-Version The next Notion-Version will make Notion-flavored Markdown ( markdown_version: "v2" ) the default on the markdown endpoints: POST /v1/pages , GET /v1/pages/:page_id/markdown , PATCH /v1/pages/:page_id/markdown , POST /v1/comments , and PATCH /v1/comments/:comment_id . On that version, requests without markdown_version will use v2 . Requests that set markdown_version to v1 will return a 400 validation_error . For now, nothing changes for requests that send a current Notion-Version . They keep enhanced markdown ( v1 ) as the default, and you can still opt in to v2 with the parameter. Enhanced markdown ( v1 ) is now deprecated. We’ll post the new version’s name and release date in this changelog before it ships. We plan to retire v1 on every Notion-Version about three months after that, and we’ll post the retirement date here at least three months ahead. To get ready, set markdown_version to v2 on your markdown requests now and test the results. See Markdown versions for where to send the parameter, and the Notion-flavored Markdown format reference for the syntax. SDK support : @notionhq/client v5.29.0 adds markdown_version to the page markdown and comment methods. Fractional credit usage in the Notion Agent APIs Credit usage fields in the Notion Agent APIs now report fractional credits, and each field rounds the same way every time. Both rules below round down. credits_used in Retrieve a session and Query sessions has at most two decimal places, so 12.456789 credits reads as 12.45 . total_credits_used in Retrieve agent insights is a whole number from 1 up, so 12.7 credits reads as 12 . Below 1, it has at most two significant figures, so 0.456789 credits reads as 0.45 . These fields were already typed as numbers. If your code assumes they’re integers, update it to handle decimals. October 29, 2026 Property IDs on property comments Comments on a database page property now include property_id , the ID of that property. It matches the property’s id in the page object . The Comment object and the comment.created , comment.updated , and comment.deleted webhook payloads carry it. Other comments omit it. SDK support : @notionhq/client v5.29.0 adds property_id to the comment response and comment webhook types. See version changes in Notion MCP notion-get-version-changes lists what changed in a page or database between two times and who changed it. See Get version changes . October 27, 2026 Suggest edits in Notion MCP Three new Notion MCP tools let an assistant propose changes that a person reviews in Notion. notion-create-suggested-edit adds a suggested edit to a page without changing its accepted content. notion-get-suggested-edit shows a pending suggestion’s before-and-after diff, and notion-resolve-suggested-edit accepts or rejects it. notion-get-comments now lists pending suggestions too. The tools need a Business or Enterprise plan. See Suggest edits . View past versions in Notion MCP notion-view-version shows a page or database as it looked at a past time. See View a past version . October 26, 2026 See connection health in the Developer portal Internal and public connections now have a Health tab in the Developer portal. It shows the connection’s API requests from the last 24 hours, including how many failed and why. A warning also appears when a connection’s requests are blocked or receive a lot of client errors or rate-limit responses. See Connection health . Open connected-source results with notion-fetch notion-fetch now opens results from notion-connector-search in hosted Notion MCP sessions. Pass a result’s id or url to read the full item, such as a Slack thread, Google Drive file, or GitHub issue. The response has the item’s title , url , and text , and metadata.type is connector . Fetch reads the item through the user’s own connection to that source, so it returns only what that connection can see. It works for Notion MCP OAuth connections and personal access tokens when the user has the same AI access as notion-connector-search . Outlook, Google Calendar, and Confluence results still can’t be fetched. See Search connected sources . Page markdown ignores pending suggested edits Retrieve a page as markdown and the notion-fetch MCP tool now show only accepted page content. Suggested edits that nobody has accepted yet no longer show up as page text. Update a page’s content as markdown and the notion-update-page MCP tool match old_str against that same view, so text you copy from a retrieved page still matches, and an edit can’t target a proposal as if it were page text. October 22, 2026 Status properties show their default option Status property schemas now include a read-only default_option . It is the name of the option a page shows when it has no explicit Status value, or null when no default is configured. Look it up in options rather than assuming the first option is the default. It appears wherever the API returns a data source’s properties, such as Retrieve a data source . In Notion MCP, notion-fetch also shows the default in each data source’s schema. SDK support : @notionhq/client v5.28.0 adds default_option to the Status property response type. October 20, 2026 Show or hide a database’s data source title Create a database , Update a database , and create_database on Create a view now accept show_data_source_title . It controls the Show data source title setting in the Notion app, which shows or hides the title above a database’s views. Database objects now include the current value. The notion-create-view MCP tool also accepts show_data_source_title when it adds a linked view to a page. See Creating a linked database view . Separate Notion and connected-source search in Notion MCP notion-search now searches only Notion pages and databases in hosted Notion MCP sessions. The new notion-connector-search tool searches connected sources such as Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, mail, and calendar. Sessions list it when the user has AI search and the workspace has a connected source. Pass sources to search only some sources. The response lists the sources it searched and warns about any source that failed or timed out. notion-ai-search no longer appears in tools/list , but it stays callable by name. Workspace-owned connections keep their selected tools. If notion-connector-search doesn’t appear, refresh the client’s tool list or reconnect Notion MCP. In ChatGPT, it appears after OpenAI reviews the updated Notion app. See Supported tools . October 16, 2026 Partial update_content edits return warnings When some update_content edits match and others don’t, Update page markdown and the notion-update-page MCP tool now apply the edits that match and list each miss in warnings with code no_match , or indentation_mismatch when the text is on the page with different indentation. This works for both markdown versions. The request fails only when no content-changing edit matches. Before, REST skipped misses without saying so, and MCP failed the whole call. See Update warnings . Property auto-fixes return warnings instead of errors in Notion MCP notion-create-pages and notion-update-page used to fail with validation_error when they auto-fixed a property, even though the fix was safe. Examples are writing URL under its data-source key userDefined:URL and coercing is_datetime to 0 or 1. Both tools now write the page and report each fix in the optional warnings array. Each notion-create-pages warning has an index that points to the page in the input. A property value that can’t be written still fails the call. Each page’s properties in the notion-create-pages result now shows what was saved, under the keys it was saved to, such as userDefined:URL , and leaves out keys the tool skipped, such as id . See Supported tools . Calendar tools in Notion MCP You can now read schedules and manage Calendar events through user-authorized Notion MCP connections on all Notion plans. See Supported tools . Icon-only and cover-only page updates in Notion MCP notion-update-page now accepts "command": "update_properties" with only icon , cover , or is_skill , so you can change a page’s icon or cover without sending properties . Before, the call returned a validation_error that said properties was required. October 15, 2026 Comment-only connections can retrieve their own bot user Retrieve your token’s bot user now works for connections that have only comment capabilities. Before this change, those connections got a 403 restricted_resource error, so they had no direct way to look up their own bot ID. October 14, 2026 Return fewer page properties from search Search now accepts the filter_properties query parameter, so you can return only the page properties you need. It works like it does on data source queries, except that search skips names or IDs that don’t exist on a page. List page backlinks in Notion MCP The new notion-list-page-backlinks tool lists the pages in the same workspace that link to or mention a page or database. It returns IDs, titles, and URLs, and only for pages the user can open. See List page backlinks . Look up permission groups in Notion MCP The new notion-get-groups tool lists the permission groups a user can see, with their IDs and names. People properties show a group only as space_permission_group-<id> , so assistants can now turn that ID into a name, or find a group by name before setting it. See Get groups . October 13, 2026 Delete pages and databases in Notion MCP Two new Notion MCP tools move content to Trash after the user confirms. notion-delete-pages moves up to 20 pages, and notion-delete-databases moves up to 20 databases with their rows. Both need the update content capability. Locked pages and databases can’t be moved to Trash. To undo a deletion, use notion-restore-pages or restore the item from Trash in Notion. See Supported tools . Edit, delete, and react to comments in Notion MCP Four new Notion MCP tools change existing comments. notion-update-comment replaces the text of a comment the user wrote, and notion-delete-comment deletes one. notion-set-discussion-resolved resolves or reopens a discussion. notion-set-comment-reaction adds or removes the user’s emoji reaction. The tools need a Business or Enterprise plan. Get comment and discussion IDs from notion-get-comments or notion-create-comment . See Supported tools . October 9, 2026 Data source schema update fixes Update a data source now changes the color of an existing select , multi_select , or status option instead of returning a validation_error . Option names also match existing options without regard to case, so sending high keeps the existing High option and its ID instead of replacing it. See Existing select options . Property updates now keep the existing description when you omit it, for every property type and when you change a type. Send null to clear it. The same rule applies to an option’s own description . Omitting options on a select or multi_select update now keeps the current options. See Update data source properties . Admin API list endpoints accept start_cursor List MCP client connections and List personal access tokens now accept start_cursor , like other Admin API list endpoints. Before this change, these endpoints ignored start_cursor and returned the first page again. The cursor parameter still works but is deprecated. If you send both with different values, the request fails with a 400 error. notion-download-skill returns markdown for Skills without files When a Skill has no supporting files, notion-download-skill in Notion MCP now returns markdown , the full SKILL.md text with its frontmatter, instead of a url to an archive. Skills with supporting files still return a signed url . See Use Notion Skills with MCP . October 8, 2026 Control notifications from page writes Page write endpoints now accept notifications.mode . Set it to silent to skip page update, @mention, and Person property notifications for the change. Database automations, reminders, and connection webhooks still work as usual. See Create a page , Update a page , and Append block children for details. October 7, 2026 One search tool in Notion MCP Hosted Notion MCP sessions now list one content-search tool, notion-search ( search for OpenAI clients). Its description matches the user’s AI search access. It describes AI search when the user has it, and keyword search otherwise, with a one-line upgrade note when the plan lacks AI search. notion-ai-search no longer appears in tools/list , but it stays callable by name, so clients with a cached tool list keep working. Workspace-owned MCP connections, which have a selected tool list, keep the earlier tool list and descriptions. In the other sessions, the server instructions also tell clients to use the Notion search tool for every content search. notion-get-tool-access is optional Except on workspace-owned connections, tool descriptions no longer tell clients to call notion-get-tool-access before they use a tool. Tools apply access limits themselves and report them in their results. Call notion-get-tool-access only when you want plan or parameter details up front. This replaces the September 17, 2026 advice to call it first. OpenAI’s search and fetch shape for ChatGPT For ChatGPT connections, a content search with search returns { results: [{ id, title, url }] } and fetch returns { id, title, text, url, metadata } , as both structuredContent and JSON text. This is the shape that OpenAI’s MCP requirements set for company knowledge and deep research. ChatGPT search results no longer include highlights, path , timestamps, or notices . When fetch gets include_file_urls: true , file download URLs are under metadata.references . User lookups and other clients don’t change; see Supported tools . Status group filters beta Status filters can now match groups with group_equals and group_does_not_equal . These operators remove option and group name ambiguity. Send Notion-Beta: status-group-filters-2026-10-06 to opt in. With the header, equals and does_not_equal match only option names. Views return saved group filters with group operators. Without the header, nothing changes. See Status group filters beta . Warnings from notion-update-page notion-update-page now returns an optional warnings array, for direct and queued updates, when it changed or ignored part of the input, such as lines dropped for incorrect indentation or text auto-corrected to match the page. Each warning has a code and a message , and Markdown parser warnings also carry category and autofix . Each message is at most 500 characters; a longer one is cut and ends with a note giving its original length. A clean update has no warnings key; see Supported tools . October 6, 2026 Personal memories in Notion MCP Connected AI clients can now save and retrieve personal memories in Notion across sessions. Use notion-memory-search to find relevant context and the existing page tools to read, create, or update memories; see Memories in Notion MCP . No more tool-specific Notion MCP rate limits notion-search and notion-query-data-sources no longer have their own rate limits. Calls to these tools now count toward the standard request limits , like other Notion MCP tools. See Supported tools . Create teamspace root pages with Notion MCP notion-create-pages now supports creating pages directly in a teamspace with parent.teamspace_id . Use a user-backed connection with permission to add top-level pages; see Teamspace root pages for details and an example. October 5, 2026 notion-fetch no longer signs file URLs by default Page markdown from notion-fetch in Notion MCP now cites files in page blocks by stable notion-file-block:// references, without signed URLs. Files in database properties are still signed inline. To get download URLs, call the new notion-get-file-download-urls tool with up to 25 references, or pass include_file_urls: true to notion-fetch . Keep the references, not the URLs, when you edit or copy page markdown. See Supported tools . October 2, 2026 Page edits return 400 when a page is too large to load Update a page’s content as markdown and the notion-update-page MCP tool now return HTTP 400 validation_error when a page is too large to load in full (about 20,000 records, most of them blocks) and the edit targets a block that wasn’t loaded or would remove content that wasn’t loaded. Before, they returned HTTP 500 internal_server_error . Retrying the same request fails the same way. Content that wasn’t loaded appears as <unknown> tags when you retrieve the page as markdown, so edit only content outside those tags. The response’s additional_data.limit_kind is page_record_count , and additional_data.limit holds the limit. September 30, 2026 Custom blocks in markdown The markdown content API and Notion MCP now read custom blocks with inherited bindings as <custom-block definition-id="…" url="…" /> instead of <unknown> . You can place existing definitions and preserve unchanged instances during page edits; see Working with markdown content . Definition creation remains in private alpha. New SIEM event for the AI meeting notes consent setting The SIEM and DLP event stream now sends workspace.settings.meeting_notes_consent_setting_updated when an admin changes whether a workspace requires consent before AI meeting notes transcription. The payload carries the final state, either enabled or disabled . See SIEM events . This is separate from the existing audit log entry for a person confirming consent in a meeting. The new event records a change to the requirement, not an instance of consent. Preview: Notion-flavored Markdown with markdown_version The markdown endpoints accept a new optional markdown_version parameter. Set it to v2 to read and write Notion-flavored Markdown. This is an opt-in preview: v1 (enhanced markdown) stays the default, and requests without the parameter work as before. Synchronous v2 updates return parser warnings . Sending markdown_version without markdown on POST /v1/pages or the comment endpoints returns a 400 validation_error . See Markdown versions and the Notion-flavored Markdown format reference . September 29, 2026 Completing the query tool update in Notion MCP notion-query-database-view is no longer available. Call notion-query-data-sources instead, and pass the same view_url as {"data": {"mode": "view", "view_url": "..."}} . Calls to the old tool name now return a tool error that names this replacement. September 28, 2026 Higher Notion MCP search and query limits Notion MCP now allows 20 search calls and 20 data source query calls per connection every 10 seconds. Rate-limit tool errors also include their structured JSON in the text response for clients that read only text. See Supported tools . September 25, 2026 Custom emoji icons are validated A custom_emoji icon on a page, database, data source, or callout must now name a custom emoji in the integration’s workspace. Otherwise the request returns a validation_error instead of saving an icon that reads back as null . See Emoji and icon . Notion MCP applies the same check to custom_emoji:<id> page icons in notion-create-pages and notion-update-page . September 24, 2026 Rate limit waits in the response body Any 429 or 529 response that includes a Retry-After header now repeats the wait in the body as additional_data.retry_after , so clients that can’t read headers, such as MCP clients, can still see how long to wait. Two new rate_limit_reason values identify an endpoint’s own limit ( public_api_endpoint_rate_limit ) and a connection whose API access has been restricted ( public_api_request_blocked ). A workspace-limit 429 now says that the limit is shared by all of the workspace’s connections. See Request limits . Page writes return 504 when a request times out Update a page’s content as markdown and the notion-update-page MCP tool now return HTTP 504 gateway_timeout when a request runs past its deadline. Before, they returned HTTP 500 internal_server_error . The notion-create-pages and notion-convert-page-to-skill MCP tools already returned 504 in this case. A 504 does not mean the write was undone, so check whether the change was saved before you retry it. A write that runs out of its time budget still returns 503 service_unavailable , with additional_data.retry_guidance . See Request limits for when to retry each status. September 23, 2026 Notion icon URLs are validated An external icon URL that points at Notion’s built-in icon set, such as https://www.notion.so/icons/pizza_blue.svg , sets a native icon and reads back as type: "icon" . A URL that names no real icon or color now returns a validation_error instead of saving a broken icon. In Notion MCP, the page icon parameter on notion-create-pages and notion-update-page now accepts the icons/pizza_blue identifier that notion-fetch returns, so an icon can be copied from one page to another. September 22, 2026 File uploads accept CAD and 3D model formats The File Upload API now accepts common CAD and 3D model formats, including .dwg , .dxf , .dwf , .rvt , .rfa , .3dm , .step , .stl , .obj , and .glb . They attach to pages as file blocks. application/octet-stream resolves from the file extension Many HTTP clients label files with application/octet-stream when they can’t infer a MIME type from the extension. Create a file upload and Send a file upload now treat that generic type as unspecified and resolve the real type from the filename extension, or from the content type set at creation. Files with unsupported extensions are still rejected. September 17, 2026 Check tool access with notion-get-tool-access Notion MCP has a new notion-get-tool-access tool. Call it with {} to get the full connection-scoped current_tool_access map. It takes an optional tool_names array such as ["search", "ai_search"] to narrow the result. Call it before you use a tool whose availability depends on the plan: to choose between notion-search and notion-ai-search , for example, or to see which parameters the workspace’s plan restricts. Those tools now say so in their descriptions, and each points to one call for the whole map that you can reuse across them. It doesn’t grant access or change the workspace. Entries in the map can now include restricted_parameters , which maps a parameter path such as filters.title_only to the reason it’s unavailable. A restriction applies even when the entry’s status is available , so check it before sending the parameter. Read the reason against your requested value: a single teamspace remains supported even when filters.teamspace_ids lists a restriction on multiple teamspaces. When ai_search is exposed and available , the map omits search , even when requested by name. Otherwise, the map can include both an available search entry and an unavailable ai_search entry, depending on the connection’s selected tools. Choose only an exposed tool. If only notion-ai-search is exposed, plan restrictions still allow its Notion-only keyword fallback; billing restrictions don’t. Search drops unavailable options instead of failing A notion-search or notion-ai-search call that asks for a filter or sort the workspace’s plan doesn’t include now runs the supported part of the search. These calls previously returned a validation_error . The response adds a notices array naming the dropped fields, with an upgrade link when available, and results can be broader than requested and use relevance sorting. On a plan without multiple-teamspace search, when teamspace_id and filters.teamspace_ids select different teamspaces, both are dropped. If dropping the options leaves an empty query with no supported constraint, the response returns no results and a notice asking for a non-empty query or a supported filter. notion-ai-search content search on a plan without AI access now runs a keyword search in Notion only rather than returning an upgrade error. It still reports type: "ai_search" and explains in notices that connected sources weren’t searched. A workspace with a billing restriction, such as an unpaid invoice, still gets a permission error asking a workspace owner to manage billing. notion-ai-search handles user lookup notion-ai-search now takes query_type . Set it to user with a name or email to look up a workspace user, and the response reports type: "user_search" , the same as notion-search . Omit query_type , or set it to internal , for a content search. Content filters and sorting aren’t valid with a user lookup and return a validation_error . A user lookup doesn’t need AI access, but both search tools need user information capabilities . Workspace-owned MCP connections must also expose notion-get-users . Choose an exposed search tool; switching tools doesn’t bypass these permissions. September 10, 2026 AI search accepts filters, and notion-search routes content queries to it notion-ai-search now accepts the exact filters and sort options that notion-search accepts, and it accepts an empty query for filter-only browsing. These options return Notion-only workspace results so the constraints are enforced exactly, and the response still reports type: "ai_search" . Omit them to search Notion and connected sources together. Filtering by editor, last-edited date, multiple teamspaces, title only, or content status, and sorting by date, still require Business or Enterprise. User lookup remains on notion-search with query_type: "user" . Content searches sent to notion-search now run AI search when the connection can use it. When notion-fetch with the id self reports current_tool_access.ai_search.status as available , a keyword content query sent to notion-search searches Notion and connected sources and reports type: "ai_search" , so clients that haven’t adopted notion-ai-search keep getting unified results. A call that passes an exact filter, an empty query, or a sort other than relevance stays on Notion workspace search. Routing respects the connection’s tool list: a connection that can’t use notion-ai-search keeps its content searches on workspace search, and the legacy content_search_mode: "ai_search" parameter returns a permission error for that connection. The 30-requests-per-minute limit on notion-search counts these calls either way. Session URL shorthand for Custom Agent session tools Notion MCP’s Custom Agent session tools now accept the shorthand session://<sessionId> and thread://<sessionId> for session_url , resolving both in the connected workspace. The full form session://<spaceId>/<sessionId> that session tools return still works, and a full URL whose workspace ID differs from the connected workspace still returns HTTP 400 validation_error . Validation and conflict errors from Custom Agent session tools Notion MCP’s Custom Agent session tools now return HTTP 400 validation_error for malformed URLs, URLs for a resource other than a session, or full URLs naming another workspace, and notion-send-message-to-session returns a conflict error when the session already has a run in progress. Both cases previously returned a generic failure. Valid URLs for missing, inaccessible, or unsupported sessions return HTTP 404 object_not_found . Wait for the run to finish with notion-wait-session before sending another message. September 9, 2026 Faster retries and plan-based rate limits The per-connection rate limit is now enforced over a fixed 60-second window: 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise plans, and 180 requests per minute on all other plans. Retry-After for this limit never exceeds 60 seconds, down from up to 15 minutes, and per-connection 429 responses now also include the wait as additional_data.retry_after in the body. See Request limits . September 2, 2026 Notion MCP splits keyword search and AI search notion-search is now keyword-only. It matches short, specific terms in Notion and no longer searches connected apps like Slack, Google Drive, and Jira. Use it for content search only when notion-fetch with the id self reports that current_tool_access.ai_search.status is not available . It remains the tool for user lookup by name or email. Semantic search moved to a new notion-ai-search tool. Use it for every content search when current_tool_access.ai_search.status is available , including searches that include specific terms. It takes one concise natural-language query and searches sources connected to the workspace, such as Slack, Mail, and Calendar, when they are available to the caller. Using it requires Notion AI; without it, calls return a prompt with a recovery link, and notion-fetch with the id self reports ai_search in current_tool_access so clients can route to notion-search . notion-ai-search does not accept the exact filters, the sort options, or the user lookup that notion-search accepts. Clients that still send the old content_search_mode parameter on notion-search keep working: workspace_search behaves like notion-search , and ai_search behaves like notion-ai-search . The parameter is no longer advertised, so call the tool you want directly. Page covers and icons in notion-fetch responses The notion-fetch MCP tool now returns cover and icon metadata for pages and database items. Both use the same shapes as the REST API, so clients can inspect the current cover or icon before deciding whether to replace it. Rich text in data source queries The notion-query-data-sources MCP tool now supports mode: "rows" to keep rich text in data source results. This mode preserves mentions and link targets that SQL output can omit. Typed databases in the REST API Create a database now accepts an optional database_type of tasks , projects , or skills . Notion builds the database from its canonical schema and metadata for that type, so the result matches a database of that type created in the Notion app. database_type can’t be combined with initial_data_source , and when title is omitted the database is named after its type. See Typed databases for the properties each type creates. Database and data source objects now include a read-only database_type field. September 1, 2026 Free workspace block limits now apply to the REST API Starting today, the REST API enforces the existing Free workspace block limit for internal connections and OAuth connections restricted to selected workspaces. This is not a new workspace limit. See Workspace block limits for the grace period, HTTP 403 response, and background template behavior. Upgrade prompts for Custom Agent tools in Notion MCP Notion MCP’s Custom Agent tools — notion-list-agents , notion-search-agents , and the session tools — now return a prompt with a recovery link when the workspace doesn’t have access to Notion AI and Custom Agents. They previously returned a generic permission error with no recovery link. notion-fetch with the id self also reports these tools as upgrade_required with an upgrade_url , or as plan_required with a landing_page_url and landing_page_action when Notion routes the user through a plan landing page. Clients can use this status to route around unavailable tools before calling. Workspaces with a billing restriction, such as an unpaid invoice, are treated separately: the tools return a permission error that asks a workspace owner to manage billing, and current_tool_access reports them as not_enabled rather than upgrade_required . A connection that lacks the “View sessions and interact with agents” capability does not advertise these tools and must reconnect or re-authorize. August 31, 2026 Capture ideas and draft content in Notion Your agent can now capture ideas and draft content in Notion without choosing where the page belongs first. The page starts as a private draft, so you can review it and organize it later. Save and reuse your preferred workflows with Notion Skills When you ask your AI to save a workflow you want to reuse, it can now create a Notion Skill or turn an existing page into one. Skills are reusable instructions stored as Notion pages that you own and can edit. When you ask for that workflow later, your AI can find the right Skill and read its instructions before starting. Find the right page more easily Your AI can now narrow Notion searches by where a page lives, who created or edited it, when it changed, whether the title matches, and the page’s status.
